propositions: Batching N candidates into one call per ordering reduces call volume from 2N to 2*ceil(N/batch), cutting system prefix copies and input tokens by ~48% against the pre-8415 baseline.

The hoisted query digest remains in the system block unchanged; the batch protocol section added to the system prompt (describing labelled-list independence and per-candidate verdicts) lifts the stable prefix from 873 to 1,337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token cache floor and enabling prompt caching.

Demultiplexing batched responses by candidate label rather than position ensures each candidate receives exactly one verdict; missing or unknown entries abstain for only that candidate without affecting others.

The change introduces precision risk via cross-contamination between neighbouring candidates in a batch; this risk is measured by running real-API parity tests showing systematic relation shifts toward conservative outcomes (mostly toward `unrelated`), with true-positive control passing at full confidence in both orderings.
